subject: general
question: Which Five-Year Plan emphasised the setting up of Basic and Heavy Industries so as to establish a strong base for rapid industrialization, self-reliance, and technological development?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Second Five - Year Plan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** placed a strong emphasis on** industrial development.**
 
• This policy was in force until the termination of the **Fifth Plan by the Janata government in 1978.**
 
• A comprehensive approach to promote **economic development, **with heavy industry at its core.
 
• The plan aimed to substitute basic and capital good industries, and various hydroelectric power projects and five steel plants were established in Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela with the assistance of foreign countries such as the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom, and West Germany.
 
• The plan also included the expansion of railway lines in the north-east region of the country.
 
• In 1957, a talent search and scholarship program was initiated to identify and train talented young students for work in the field of nuclear power.
 
• The objective of the program was to build a skilled workforce that would support the country's push towards industrialization and modernization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five - Year Plan****​**

 
 
• ​The planning ethos underpinned the Indian economy from 1947 to 2017. The **Planning Commission (1951–2014)** and the** NITI Aayog** devised, carried out, and supervised this through the **Five-Year Plans. (2015-2017).**
 
• The commission has a nominated deputy chairman who is a cabinet minister, with the prime minister serving as the ex-officio chairman. The commission's last deputy chairman is **Montek Singh Ahluwalia**. (resigned on 26 May 2014). In March 2017, the **Twelfth Plan's tenure **came to an end.
 
• The Gadgil formula was adopted in 1969 as a result of the distribution of state resources prior to the Fourth Plan being based on schematic patterns rather than a transparent and objective procedure.
